title: Rust multi_instance.rs: RootCandidate sanitizes NaN only, +inf/-inf RF metrics poison select_root
description: Found in C port review (b7z9.24.2). rust/lichen-rpl/src/multi_instance.rs:927-943 with_rf_metrics/with_rssi_ema/with_snr_ema sanitize with is_nan() only; rssi_ema = f32::INFINITY passes sanitize, combined_score 2*INF + snr wins the score criterion over all finite candidates whenever preference/stratum tie, so a malformed/poisoned beacon metric can force root selection. C port (tdma_root_select.c) now treats all non-finite as worst-case (-120/-20 -> score -260). Fix Rust: replace is_nan() with !is_finite() in the three setters (NaN and inf both map to worst-case defaults), add a test pinning INF rejection. Note: may cross-check python slot_coordination.py for the same gap.
close_reason: Landed per the bead: the three RootCandidate builder setters (with_rf_metrics/with_rssi_ema/with_snr_ema in lichen-rpl/src/multi_instance.rs) now sanitize ALL non-finite values (is_finite() guard replacing is_nan() — NaN, +inf, -inf all map to the worst-case defaults -120.0/-20.0), mirroring C tdma_root_select.c exactly. New test additions in root_candidate_nan_rf_metrics_sanitized: INF/-INF sanitization pins for both metrics, Eq reflexivity for non-finite inputs, and an ordering pin (a +inf-poisoned candidate LOSES to a finite candidate under identical preference/stratum — the actual 'must not win root selection' behavior). Also fixed en route: removed a duplicate IPV6_IN_IPV6 const (lichen-core/src/ipv6.rs:28, an E0428 compile break from a bad main sync). Verified: lichen-rpl 248+13 green, clippy --all-features -D warnings clean, fmt clean. Reviews: correctness PASS, security PASS (defaults match C's -120/-20, score floor -260 matches the C clamp, Ord stays total via total_cmp, no builder bypass in-tree), edge-cases found the finite-extreme gap (f32::MAX passes is_finite and still wins) — beyond the mirror-C scope, filed as its own cross-impl parity bead (clamp to the plausible RF domain in both implementations).
